clue.text: Like a farmer with belly-ache after badly undercooked starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the words badly and undercooked

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain, a belly-ache

explanation.surface: A farmer doubled up with stomach pains after eating half-raw food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes the first letters of 'badly undercooked', B and U, which come before COLIC as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes rural, pastoral country life, the world of a farmer.

clue.text: Raleigh's early days on canvas?

parts.note: Millais painted Walter Raleigh as a youngster listening to a sailor's tales; the picture's title names his youth

explanation.walkthrough: 'on canvas' might suggest camping, but it means a painting: Millais's famous picture of the young Raleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Early days are one's youth, the years before manhood, as in the title of Millais's painting.

clue.text: This account serves as a warning

definitions.text: This account serves as a warning

parts.words: This account serves as a warning
parts.note: a story told to warn listeners of danger, with a moral attached

explanation.definitionFit: A story with a moral that warns of the consequences of folly, like Belloc's verses for children.

clue.text: Final place for Oxford, say

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a style of shoe, and a cobbler shapes shoes on a foot-shaped block

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' is not the university but a lace-up shoe, made on a cobbler's block.
explanation.definitionFit: The final item comes at the end; a cobbler's foot-shaped block holds a shoe such as an Oxford.

clue.text: Toady sort of slow swimmer

definitions.meaning: a sycophant who fawns on superiors
something that moves slowly through water, playing on the front crawl stroke

explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns and creeps; a slow mover creeps along, and front crawl is a swimming stroke.

clue.text: Pinch of snuff?

parts.note: not a dose of tobacco: pinching a candle wick snuffs the flame, which halts or ends it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a small quantity of powdered tobacco; read instead as the act of pinching out a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff a candle is to put an end to its burning, and a pinch of the fingers does just that.

clue.text: Leaves-tennis abandoned!

definitions.meaning: the sets of a tennis match called off

explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to depart on a journey; tennis matches abandoned have their sets called off.

clue.text: Dummies found in ruined sofa

indicators.note: ruined tells us the letters of sofa are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Idiots discovered lounging on a wrecked settee.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, stupid people are louts or dimwits, informally called dummies.

clue.text: Kind of ball sometimes held in a tent?

definitions.text: Kind of ball sometimes held in a tent?

parts.words: Kind of ball sometimes held in a tent?
parts.note: not a dance in a marquee: the glass sphere a fortune-teller gazes into in a fairground booth

explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance in a marquee; it is the clairvoyant's glass globe at the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller at a fair peers into a glass globe to read the future.

clue.text: Wrestling with a shift is no trouble at all

parts.note: all-in is a freestyle form of wrestling
a shift is a period of labour, one day's work

explanation.surface: Grappling during your shift is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Something routine and expected is part of normal duties, causing no trouble at all.

clue.text: How some people remain in business?

definitions.text: How some people remain in business?

parts.words: How some people remain in business?
parts.note: not staying in trade: the formal sign-off people use at the end of business letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'remain' plays on the closing formula of a letter, where a writer remains the addressee's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the conventional valediction for formal correspondence opened with 'Dear Sir'.

clue.text: Roman poet has four in party, when retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the whole assembled piece is read from right to left
in tells us the numeral sits inside the word for party

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Roman poet goes to a party with four friends but leaves early.
explanation.walkthrough: IV inside DO makes DIVO, and 'when retiring' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, author of the Metamorphoses, was a celebrated poet of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Some high-level language in the local golf-club

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words local golf-club

explanation.surface: Members chat in a jargon of their own at the local golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'locAL GOLf'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algol, short for Algorithmic Language, is an early high-level computer programming language.

clue.text: Film to be avoided, would you say?

indicators.note: would you say asks us to go by how the word for avoided is spoken

parts.note: something avoided has been missed

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a particular movie is best skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is not a movie but a thin layer, as of condensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin film of water droplets on glass or in the air is a haze of condensation.

clue.text: Bonnie's companion-flower

definitions.meaning: Bonnie Parker's partner in crime in 1930s America
a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Scottish river through Glasgow

explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, as a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow was Bonnie Parker's outlaw partner; the Scottish river through Glasgow also bears the name.

clue.text: Tin box for an imaginary animal

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an ark is a chest or box

explanation.surface: A tin container for a creature of fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's mock-heroic poem describes a hunt for this invented creature.

clue.text: Day-fisherman who hangs loose

parts.note: an angler is a fisherman with rod and line

explanation.surface: A relaxed weekend fisherman takes life easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangling hangs or swings loosely, so one that does so is a dangling thing.

clue.text: Pigeon with a cooler rump?

parts.note: a fan cools people down
the rump is the hindquarters, the tail end

explanation.surface: A bird with a chilly backside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of domestic pigeon with a spread, fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Retriever-one that lays next to shadow

parts.note: a bird is a creature that lays eggs
to shadow someone is to dog their steps, following closely

explanation.surface: A gun dog belonging to an egg-laying hen follows close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' simply places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American term for a gun dog trained to fetch shot game birds.

clue.text: Group to fight for somewhere to put a bowler

parts.note: a band is a group, as of musicians
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A team is eager to fight for a place for their bowler on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' is not a cricketer but a hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A light cardboard box is used for storing hats such as a bowler.

clue.text: Chap taking in a marine jacket, for example

indicators.note: taking in means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a gentleman
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A man takes in a Royal Marine's jacket for alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts A and RM inside GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one example of an item of clothing.

clue.text: Does she set up counter-measures?

parts.note: not defensive action: a woman who pours out measures of drink across a pub counter

explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-measures' reads as tactics until split: measures of spirits served at a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: She serves drinks from behind the bar of a pub, pouring each tot.

clue.text: Mars shows a billion flashes

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for billion
flashes are bursts of light

explanation.surface: The red planet shows countless twinkling points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet but is a verb: spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil it, as a disease spoils crops.

clue.text: Actor's assistant with his back to the wall

definitions.meaning: the person who helps a performer into costume backstage

definitions.text: with his back to the wall
definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with shelves stands against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper aids performers with costumes; a kitchen sideboard stands against a wall.

clue.text: Record token

definitions.meaning: to record something is to write it down
a banknote is a token of value

explanation.definitionFit: To jot something down is to record it; a promissory slip or banknote is a token of money owed.

clue.text: Bishop to attack scrambled egg

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A bishop goes for his breakfast eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled egg' is military slang for the gold lace on a senior officer's cap peak, not a breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers' gold ornamental trimming is nicknamed after a breakfast dish because of how it looks.

clue.text: Former Wimbledon champion has changed direction

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of has are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An old tennis star has taken a new course in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns HAS into ASH, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, the American player, won the men's singles at Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Cold shoulder and teacakes put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: buns are sweet teacakes

explanation.surface: Someone ignored offers teacakes on a high shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the cold shoulder is to rebuff or ignore someone deliberately.

clue.text: Double reed blown in the wind

definitions.text: Double reed blown in the wind

parts.words: Double reed blown in the wind
parts.note: a woodwind instrument whose mouthpiece is a pair of reeds, played in the wind section

explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' is the orchestra's wind section, not a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the double-reed woodwind instrument that gives the orchestra its tuning A.

clue.text: Accountant's aim, to train like a model?

definitions.meaning: making the debits and credits in the ledgers agree
deportment practice by walking with volumes resting on one's head

explanation.definitionFit: An accountant wants the ledgers to agree; models learned poise by walking with volumes perched on their heads.

clue.text: A stake in Lincoln Square

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of Abraham Lincoln
a T-square is a draughtsman's square, giving T

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager in a town square in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stake' also reads as A plus BET, a stake, so the clue works two ways; 'stake' as a verb means to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To stake a plant is to prop it up, and to aid someone is to back or support them.

clue.text: He may call for order in diet

definitions.text: He may call for order in diet

parts.words: He may call for order in diet
parts.note: not a dieter ordering food: the presiding officer of a legislature such as a Diet calls members to order

explanation.walkthrough: A Diet is a national assembly, as in Japan; its chair cries 'Order!' like the chair of the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The presiding officer of a parliament keeps debate orderly and calls members to order.
